concepts.name: Looking far away is looking back in time
concepts.statement: Light from a distant galaxy has been on its way for as many years as the galaxy is light years away, so the farther we look, the older the universe we see.

concepts.name: The cosmological red shift is the stretching of light by the expansion of space
concepts.statement: The cosmological red shift is the stretching of the wavelength of light by the expansion of space while the light travels. Nearly every galaxy shows a red shift proportional to its distance; it is not a Doppler shift, and every observer sees the other galaxies receding.

concepts.name: Hubble's law, $\kv = H_{0}\kd$
concepts.statement: The recession velocity of a galaxy is proportional to its distance, $v = H_{0}d$, where the constant of proportionality $H_{0}$ is the Hubble constant.

concepts.name: Find a galaxy's recession speed from its distance, or its distance from its speed
concepts.statement: Hubble's law turns a galaxy's distance into its recession speed and a recession speed, measured from a red shift, into a distance. The same arithmetic gives a rough age of the universe.

concepts.name: The cosmic microwave background is the cooled remnant of the Big Bang
concepts.statement: The cosmic microwave background is blackbody radiation at about 2.7 K that fills all of space, the remnant of the hot early universe stretched to long wavelengths by its expansion. Its discovery is the second great piece of evidence for the Big Bang.

concepts.name: A small asymmetry in the forces left the universe made of matter
concepts.statement: The universe is nearly pure matter, although particle physics is almost symmetric between matter and antimatter. A tiny asymmetry of the forces in the early universe left a little matter over when the rest annihilated.

concepts.name: The small wrinkles in the cosmic microwave background
concepts.statement: The cosmic microwave background shows tiny variations, or wrinkles, from one direction to another. Galaxies could not have formed without such early fluctuations in density, and yet the background is so smooth that its smoothness needs an explanation.

concepts.name: The epochs of the early universe follow the unification of the forces
concepts.statement: Going back in time, the universe grows hotter and denser until the average particle energy reaches the energies at which the forces unify. The TOE, GUT and electroweak epochs are named for those unifications.

concepts.name: Spontaneous symmetry breaking and the inflationary scenario
concepts.statement: When the strong force separated from the electroweak force, the transition released energy that may have expanded the universe by a factor of $10^{50}$ or more in an instant. That inflation would stretch the early wrinkles nearly flat and so explain the smoothness of the background radiation.

concepts.name: Cosmology
concepts.statement: Cosmology is the study of the character and evolution of the universe.

concepts.name: The Big Bang
concepts.statement: The Big Bang is the hot, dense beginning from which the universe has been expanding ever since, about 14 billion years ago.

concepts.name: The Hubble constant $H_{0}$
concepts.statement: The Hubble constant $H_{0}$ is the ratio of a galaxy's recession velocity to its distance, the slope of a graph of one against the other, about 20 (km/s)/Mly.

concepts.name: Superforce
concepts.statement: The superforce is the single unified force that the four basic forces are thought to have been at the highest energies of the early universe.

concepts.name: TOE epoch
concepts.statement: The TOE epoch is the time before about $10^{-43}$ s after the Big Bang, when all four forces were unified in the superforce.

concepts.name: GUT epoch
concepts.statement: The GUT epoch is the time after gravity separated, when the strong, weak and electromagnetic forces were still unified, ending about $10^{-35}$ s after the Big Bang.

concepts.name: Electroweak epoch
concepts.statement: The electroweak epoch is the time after the strong force separated, when the weak and electromagnetic forces were still unified, ending about $10^{-11}$ s after the Big Bang.

concepts.name: Spontaneous symmetry breaking
concepts.statement: Spontaneous symmetry breaking is the separation of a unified force into distinct forces as the universe cools, a transition that releases energy, as water releases energy when it freezes.

concepts.name: The inflationary scenario
concepts.statement: The inflationary scenario holds that the energy released when the strong force separated from the electroweak force expanded the universe by a factor of $10^{50}$ or more in an instant, stretching the early wrinkles nearly flat.

concepts.name: Acceleration and gravity produce identical effects
concepts.statement: A person in a closed elevator cannot tell whether it accelerates upward or stands in a gravitational field. Einstein took this to hold in all situations, and general relativity grows from it.

concepts.name: Gravity bends the path of light
concepts.statement: Light has no mass, yet its path bends in a gravitational field, because mass curves space and light follows the curve. Its observation in the 1919 eclipse was the first verification of general relativity.

concepts.name: Gravitational lensing
concepts.statement: Gravitational lensing is the bending of light from a distant galaxy by the gravity of a nearer one, which acts like a converging lens and can form several images. It is a large-scale test of general relativity.

concepts.name: Black holes and the event horizon
concepts.statement: An object whose escape velocity exceeds the speed of light lets nothing out. The event horizon is the distance at which the escape velocity is exactly the speed of light, and it is the edge of the black hole.

concepts.name: The Schwarzschild radius, $\kRS = 2GM/\kc^{2}$
concepts.statement: The radius of the event horizon of a black hole is $R_{\text{S}} = 2GM/c^{2}$, in proportion to its mass. Since $G$ is small and $c^{2}$ is large, a black hole of a few solar masses is only a few kilometers across.

concepts.name: Find the Schwarzschild radius of a black hole of a given mass
concepts.statement: The Schwarzschild radius $R_{\text{S}} = 2GM/c^{2}$ turns the mass of a black hole into the size of its event horizon, from a stellar black hole to a supermassive one at a galaxy's core.

concepts.name: Neutron stars are the collapsed cores of supernovas
concepts.statement: In a supernova the core's electrons and protons are forced together into neutrons, and the strong force halts the collapse at a star of nuclear density. A neutron star is slightly larger than a black hole of the same mass.

concepts.name: Gravitational waves
concepts.statement: Gravitational waves are ripples in the curvature of space itself, sent out by moving masses as a water bug's foot sends waves across a pond. They travel at the speed of light and only extreme events make them strong enough to detect.

concepts.name: Quantum gravity and the radiation of black holes
concepts.statement: Where gravity is strong enough to act on the quantum scale, quantum mechanics and general relativity must be used together. A black hole can then radiate, as pairs created near its horizon split and one member escapes.

concepts.name: General relativity
concepts.statement: General relativity is Einstein's theory of gravitation, in which mass curves space and time and the curvature governs the motion of matter and light.

concepts.name: Thought experiment
concepts.statement: A thought experiment is an experiment carried out in the mind rather than with apparatus, to reason out what a theory implies.

concepts.name: Escape velocity
concepts.statement: The escape velocity of a body is the smallest speed an object must have at its surface to escape the body's gravity entirely.

concepts.name: Black hole
concepts.statement: A black hole is an object so dense that its escape velocity exceeds the speed of light, so that nothing, not even light, can escape from it.

concepts.name: Event horizon
concepts.statement: The event horizon is the distance from a black hole at which the escape velocity equals the speed of light; nothing inside it can get out.

concepts.name: Quasar
concepts.statement: A quasar is an extremely distant and luminous object, thought to be the center of a young galaxy powered by a supermassive black hole.

concepts.name: Quantum gravity
concepts.statement: Quantum gravity is the theory, not yet found, that would describe gravity where it is strong enough to act on the quantum scale, by joining quantum mechanics and general relativity.

concepts.name: Superstring theory treats fundamental particles as vibrating strings
concepts.statement: Superstring theory is an attempt at a Theory of Everything, and so must contain quantum gravity. Its particles, the graviton among them, act like one-dimensional vibrating strings in a superspace whose extra dimensions curled up as the forces separated.

concepts.name: There may be a smallest length and a shortest time
concepts.statement: Quantum gravity suggests that space and time are grainy, with no meaning to intervals shorter than some tiny finite size. Superstrings would sit at that limit, with no further substructure.

concepts.name: Galaxies rotate with a nearly flat velocity curve
concepts.statement: The orbital speed of the stars in a galaxy stays almost constant out to great distances from its center, instead of falling off as it would if the galaxy's mass were concentrated, like its luminous stars, near the center. This flat rotation curve is the first evidence for dark matter.

concepts.name: Dark matter
concepts.statement: Dark matter is matter that cannot be seen but whose gravity shows it is there; there is about ten times as much of it in the universe as there is luminous matter, and what it is remains unknown.

concepts.name: The critical density, $\krhoc \approx 10^{-26}\;\text{kg/m}^{3}$
concepts.statement: The critical density $\rho_{\text{c}} \approx 10^{-26}\;\text{kg/m}^{3}$ is the average density of the universe that would just halt its expansion in a universe with no cosmological constant, a few nucleons per cubic meter.

concepts.name: Open, closed and flat universes
concepts.statement: An open universe is negatively curved and expands forever, a closed one is positively curved and returns a traveler to the start, and a flat one lies between. Measurements show the universe is very close to flat.

concepts.name: MACHOs and microlensing
concepts.statement: MACHOs, small dark bodies in a galaxy's halo, would not block a star's light but would focus it as they pass in front of it, and the star would brighten in a characteristic manner. Searches for such microlensing test whether dark matter is ordinary matter.

concepts.name: Neutrino oscillations and neutrino mass
concepts.statement: A neutrino can change from one flavor to another only if it has mass, since a massless neutrino travels at the speed of light and no time passes for it. Oscillations explain the missing solar neutrinos and could supply some of the dark matter.

concepts.name: WIMPs, previously unknown particles as dark matter
concepts.statement: WIMPs are proposed weakly interacting massive particles, chargeless and of a completely new kind, that could make up dark matter. They would gather in halos rather than coalesce into spirals.

concepts.name: Cosmological constant
concepts.statement: The cosmological constant is a term in Einstein's equations of general relativity that acts as a repulsion causing the expansion of the universe to accelerate.

concepts.name: Negatively curved universe
concepts.statement: A negatively curved universe is an open one, curved like a saddle, in which the angles of a large triangle add to less than $180^{\circ}$ and the expansion continues forever.

concepts.name: Positively curved universe
concepts.statement: A positively curved universe is a closed one, curved like a sphere, in which the angles of a large triangle add to more than $180^{\circ}$ and a traveler going straight returns to the start.

concepts.name: Flat universe
concepts.statement: A flat universe has zero curvature, so that the angles of a triangle add to exactly $180^{\circ}$; it lies between an open and a closed universe.

concepts.name: MACHOs
concepts.statement: MACHOs, massive compact halo objects, are dark bodies of ordinary matter, such as faint stars and planets, in a galaxy's halo, proposed as part of the dark matter.

concepts.name: Microlensing
concepts.statement: Microlensing is the brightening of a distant star when a small dark body passes in front of it and focuses its light by gravitational lensing.

concepts.name: Axions
concepts.statement: Axions are a proposed kind of light, weakly interacting particle that could make up some of the dark matter.

concepts.name: Neutralinos
concepts.statement: Neutralinos are proposed neutral, weakly interacting massive particles predicted by some theories, candidates for the dark matter.

concepts.name: Complexity, the study of complex adaptive systems
concepts.statement: Complexity is the study of complex adaptive systems, those that obey the simple laws of physics yet can adapt, organize themselves and evolve.

concepts.name: Chaos is extreme sensitivity to initial conditions
concepts.statement: Chaos is a system's extreme sensitivity to its initial conditions, so that a small change in where it starts changes its outcome tremendously and its long-term behavior cannot be predicted with precision.

concepts.name: Chaos can hold order and self-organization
concepts.statement: There can be organization in chaos, and it can be quantified. Some chaotic systems settle into a stable self-organized form.

concepts.name: High-temperature superconductors
concepts.statement: High-temperature superconductors are ceramics, found since 1986, that superconduct above 77 K, the boiling point of cheap liquid nitrogen, which makes them economically interesting.

concepts.name: A superconductor excludes magnetic flux
concepts.statement: A superconductor keeps magnetic flux out and so repels a magnet. A magnet floating above a cooled sample is the evidence that it is superconducting.

concepts.name: Compare the cost of cooling a superconductor with the energy a normal wire wastes
concepts.statement: A superconducting wire pays only when cooling it costs less than the energy a normal wire loses to heat, a comparison made with the power dissipated in a resistance and the price of electric energy.

concepts.name: Forefront results must be reproducible
concepts.statement: A result at the frontier is accepted only when it can be reproduced or is of such quality that a single observation is meaningful. Reports of superconductors above 200 K have not passed that test.

concepts.name: Critical temperature $T_{\text{c}}$
concepts.statement: The critical temperature $T_{\text{c}}$ of a superconductor is the temperature at and below which it has zero resistivity.

concepts.name: Open questions on the largest, intermediate and smallest scales
concepts.statement: The open questions of physics lie on three scales, the largest, the intermediate and the smallest, and each rests on physics already known.

concepts.name: The largest and smallest scales answer each other
concepts.statement: Many of the open questions of cosmology have answers in particle physics, and the reverse. The closure of the universe, for example, depends on the type and number of particles that may contribute to it.
